row.notes: In Sess_Ai_BuildVehicleRecords: mov rax,[rsp+0x118] (8 bytes), the load of the local vector's begin pointer right before mov rax,[rax] at 0x1438a41bc, the first read of the first found asset-group node. rax=0 and the fault is reading 0x0 when no asset group held the vehicle's name. Core's session enter guard tests [rsp+0x118] here; rsp is the function's own frame (it is not changed between the prologue and here); [rsp+0x30] is the manager.  UNUSED since PR #676 round 2: the skip (rbx=[rsp+0x30], rip=VehicleNext) drops the vehicle's record and shifts the slot-indexed records at [mgr+0x128] (V8614). Core now fixes the name hash at site_Sess_AiRecords_NameHash instead.

verify.notes: V8614 sigcheck hits=1 target=0x1438a41b4 and the load is [rsp+0x118] as claimed. But the guard that skips the vehicle is not safe: the produced vector at [mgr+0x128] is read as records[vehicleSlot*0x188] by FUN_1438aa730 and FUN_1438aa930 (called from FUN_142f32ad0 and FUN_142882f00 with a vehicle byte) and by FUN_1438a8b30 and FUN_1438a9250 via [[mgr+0x128]+0x48+slot*0x188]. A skipped vehicle shifts every later record by one and the last slots read past the vector end. Only FUN_1438a4f70 iterates positionally (it takes the slot from record+0x3c). Do not hook as a skip; keep one record per slot (see the vehicle_next row).
